evals.name: basics-experiments
evals.prompt: I'm using the vaswani test collection in PyTerrier. Set up BM25 and DPH retrievers, plus a third system that's BM25 top-100 rescored by a custom transformer which adds a bonus of +1.0 to the BM25 score for any document whose text contains the first term of the query (needs the document text). Compare all three in one pt.Experiment with nDCG@10, MAP and RR@10, with the BM25 as baseline, a paired t-test and Bonferroni correction. Then do a small grid search of BM25's b over {0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9} on the vaswani topics using the experiments skill's tuning guidance and report the best b with its nDCG@10. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: One script; custom transformer passes pt.inspect checks; Experiment with baseline=0, correction='bonferroni'; grid search via pt.GridSearch or a loop; results table.
expectations: The custom transformer starts transform() with a pt.validate call and passes pt.inspect.transformer_inputs/outputs
The bonus transformer returns row["score"] + 1.0 for matching documents, not a bare 1.0/0.0
pt.Experiment is called with baseline=0 and a correction argument
The text column is added with a text_loader before the custom scorer
No legacy API (pt.init, BatchRetrieve) appears in the script
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: huggingface-retrieval
evals.prompt: I want to run BM25 on BEIR nfcorpus (irds:beir/nfcorpus/test) in PyTerrier. First check whether there's a prebuilt Terrier or PISA index for nfcorpus on Hugging Face and load it with pt.Artifact.from_hf if so; otherwise build a Terrier index locally from the corpus. Then ALSO build a PISA index locally of the same corpus, and run BM25 on both with identical k1=0.9, b=0.4 so the scores are comparable. Fuse the two runs with reciprocal rank fusion. Evaluate Terrier BM25, PISA BM25 and the fusion on the nfcorpus test topics with nDCG@10 and R@100 in one pt.Experiment. Finally show me how I'd push my local Terrier index to Hugging Face (don't actually push, just the code). Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: Script that looks for an artifact, builds Terrier and PISA indexes with matching parameters, fuses with pta.RRFusion, evaluates, and shows index.to_hf(...) code.
expectations: Punctuation (at least ':') is stripped from the queries before the Terrier retriever
The two backends are compared by rank or fused by rank, never by score
Fusion follows the pyterrier-fusion skill (RRFusion), with pyterrier-retrieval for the indexes
k1 and b are passed explicitly to both backends
Fusion uses RRFusion, not raw score addition
The push code uses the artifact to_hf API without executing it
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: reranking-caching
evals.prompt: On vaswani in PyTerrier: take BM25 top-50 and rerank with (a) the sentence-transformers cross-encoder cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 and (b) monoT5 (castorini/monot5-base-msmarco-10k) — CPU only, so restrict to the first 15 topics. Wrap both rerankers in a pyterrier-caching scorer cache so that re-running the Experiment is near-instant and prove it with timings. Then separately train a learning-to-rank model with LightGBM using BM25, DPH and PL2 scores as features (feature union), training on half the vaswani topics and testing on the other half. Evaluate everything with nDCG@10 and MAP in pt.Experiment with BM25 as baseline. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: Script with text_loader before rerankers, ScorerCache around each scorer, timing evidence of cache hits, a ** feature union with LightGBM fit on a topic split, one Experiment.
expectations: A text column is added before each reranker
The cache wraps the scorer and the second run is measurably faster
LTR trains on one topic subset and evaluates on a disjoint subset
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: expansion-rag
evals.prompt: Two things in PyTerrier on vaswani. (1) Compare BM25 against BM25 with RM3 and BM25 with Bo1 pseudo-relevance feedback (fb_terms=10, fb_docs=3), and also a doc2query-- style document expansion on a 200-document slice using a small T5 doc2query model if the skill shows how (skip with a note if it needs a GPU). Evaluate with nDCG@10 and MAP and show the rewritten query for topic 1 with the original restored afterwards. (2) Build a small retrieval-augmented generation pipeline: BM25 top-3 with document text, fed to a small seq2seq reader (google/flan-t5-small is fine on CPU) that answers the question, and run it on 3 vaswani topics printing the generated answers. If pyterrier-rag has an evaluation measure for generated answers, show how it would be used. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: Script with RM3/Bo1 pipelines using pt.rewrite.reset() after expansion, optional doc2query on a slice, a pyterrier-rag reader pipeline printing answers, and a note on RAG measures.
expectations: RM3 and Bo1 are followed by the retriever and pt.rewrite.reset() restores query_0
The RAG pipeline is run over the 3 topics with .transform(topics), not .search()
The RAG reader receives qid, query and text columns and produces an answer column
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: dense-splade
evals.prompt: On a 60-document slice of vaswani, index with a small dense encoder (pick the cheapest the skill offers on CPU; sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via pyterrier-dr if the skill supports arbitrary sentence-transformers models) and retrieve for 2 queries; then use the same model as a scorer to rerank BM25 top-10; then run vector PRF. Do the same slice with SPLADE (naver/splade-cocondenser-ensembledistil) into a PISA index with the skill's recommended settings and retrieve for the same 2 queries, then use splade.scorer() to rerank BM25 top-10.
evals.expected_output: Two small scripts; FlexIndex built once and queried with the same encoder; VectorPrf after vec_loader; SPLADE PISA index built with stemmer='none' and queried via quantized(); scorer reranks after text_loader.
expectations: The BM25 first stage for the rerank is built over the 60-document slice, or the full prebuilt vaswani BM25 is stated to be a stand-in
SPLADE returning fewer than 60 documents is explained as zero-score documents being omitted
The dense query encoder is the same model as the document encoder
The SPLADE PISA index is created with stemmer='none'
Each scorer is preceded by a text loader
The scripts run to completion in the project venv

evals.name: colbert-pylate
evals.prompt: I want to try lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1 in PyTerrier through PyLate (lightonai/pyterrier-pylate). Set up whatever Python environment it needs without breaking the project venv. On a 60-document slice of vaswani, build a PLAID index with it and retrieve for 2 vaswani queries. Then rerank BM25 top-10 for the same 2 queries in two ways: from the embeddings in the PLAID index, and from the document text without the index; explain why the two rerankers return different numbers of rows. Tell me whether I could also load the prebuilt pyterrier/vaswani.colbertv2 index in the same environment, and show (don't run) how I'd share my PLAID index on Hugging Face so others query it with the right model.
evals.expected_output: A separate venv with pyterrier-pylate installed from git; a script that indexes the slice with doc_encoder() >> PlaidIndex, retrieves with query_encoder() >> index.retriever(k), reranks with query_encoder() >> index.scorer() and text_loader() >> text_scorer(); an explanation that index.scorer() drops candidates outside the 60 indexed documents; a no to loading .colbertv2 (pyterrier_colbert2, transformers<5); and index.to_hf(...) code with the model name recorded on the card.
expectations: The two vaswani queries are retrieved with .transform(topics) and keep distinct qids
The PyLate environment installs pyterrier[java] (or pyterrier[all]) so the Terrier BM25 works
The transformers requirement is stated as pylate's pin (<=5.3), not as 'transformers 5'
pyterrier-pylate is installed from git into a separate environment, not with `pip install pyterrier-pylate` and not into the project venv
model.query_encoder() comes before index.retriever() and index.scorer()
A text loader comes before model.text_scorer()
The answer says index.scorer() drops BM25 candidates that are not in the 60-document index
The answer says the .colbertv2 index needs pyterrier_colbert2, which needs transformers<5 and so a different environment
The sharing code uses index.to_hf(...) and records the model name, since the index does not store it
The scripts run to completion in the new environment

evals.name: local-index-punctuation
evals.prompt: I want to understand how much the lexical backend matters on BEIR scifact (irds:beir/scifact/test) in PyTerrier, with indexes I build myself (don't download prebuilt ones). Build a Terrier index locally with the default indexer settings, a second Terrier index with stemmer="EnglishSnowballStemmer", and a PISA index of the same corpus. Run BM25 with k1=0.9, b=0.4 on all test topics on all three (several topics contain ':' and other punctuation, keep them all), and give me nDCG@10 and R@100 in one pt.Experiment with the default Terrier index as baseline. Also report, per backend, how many topics returned no results, and the mean top-10 overlap between each pair of backends. Before indexing, print one document so I can see the field names. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: One script: three local indexes, a pt.apply.query punctuation strip before the Terrier retrievers, k1/b passed explicitly to every bm25(), one Experiment with baseline and correction, empty-result counts and pairwise top-10 overlap computed by rank.
expectations: Punctuation is stripped before the Terrier retrievers, and no run is aborted by IllegalStateException or Unknown field
k1 and b are passed explicitly to all three bm25() calls
The first document is printed with a for loop or iter(), not next() on get_corpus_iter()
Backends are compared by rank (overlap), and scores are not claimed to be comparable
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: suiteeval-lazy-cache
evals.prompt: Using PyTerrier and SuiteEval, run two systems over the NanoBEIR scifact and nfcorpus datasets: BM25, and BM25 top-20 reranked by monoELECTRA (pyterrier_dr.ElectraScorer, CPU only). Use index_dir and save_dir so indexes and runs are reused. Wrap the reranker in a pyterrier-caching scorer cache with a lazily loaded model so that running the script a second time loads no model at all; prove it with the cache's hit/miss output and wall time for both runs. Report nDCG@10 per dataset and the Overall row, with BM25 as baseline. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: One script: NanoBEIR(pipelines, eval_metrics=[nDCG@10], index_dir=..., save_dir=..., subset or two datasets), named pipelines, index.built() check, ScorerCache around text_loader >> Lazy model with declared columns, verbose=True hit/miss lines, two timed runs.
expectations: Pipelines yielded by the factory are named and the factory checks index.built() before indexing
The scorer cache wraps the text loader and the model, and the Lazy model declares transform_outputs (or equivalent) so a fully cached run loads no model
The second run reports 0 misses and is measurably faster
The suite is called as NanoBEIR(pipelines, ...), not as a class
The script runs to completion in the project venv

evals.name: fusion
evals.prompt: On the first 500 documents of vaswani in PyTerrier (CPU only): build a BM25 index over just those 500 documents and a dense FlexIndex over the same documents with sentence-transformers BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 through pyterrier-dr, deciding and justifying whether the index needs sim_fn="cos". Retrieve for the first 10 vaswani topics with both. Then fuse them two ways: reciprocal rank fusion, and a weighted score interpolation whose weight you choose on topics 11-30 and apply to topics 1-10. Separately, take BM25 top-20 over the 500 documents, rerank it with cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 and with the dense model as a scorer, and fuse those two reranked lists with RRF without running BM25 twice. Evaluate every single system and every fusion on topics 1-10 in one pt.Experiment (nDCG@10, MAP) with BM25 as baseline. Give me one script I can re-run.
evals.expected_output: One script: slice index for both backends, SBertBiEncoder with a norm check or a justified sim_fn, retrieval via .transform(topics), pta.RRFusion and a per-query min-max interpolation (not pta.fusion.PerQueryMaxMinScore, which is broken), weight chosen on held-out topics, rerankers over a cached or frame-fused BM25 top-20, one Experiment with baseline and correction.
expectations: sim_fn is justified with a norm check or model evidence, and the same encoder is used for documents and queries
No raw score addition: fusion is RRF or normalised interpolation, and pta.fusion.PerQueryMaxMinScore is not used (or its ImportError is handled)
The interpolation weight is chosen on topics other than the reported ones
The reranker fusion does not run BM25 twice (RetrieverCache, or rr_fusion on result frames)
The dense rerank uses model.scorer() after a text loader
All queries are run with .transform(topics), and the script runs to completion in the project venv
